capital.zh: 普利斯卡，893年起为普雷斯拉夫，后为奥赫里德

summary.en: Founded by Asparukh's Bulgars south of the Danube, the state merged Turkic Bulgar elites with Slavic farmers. Under Krum and Simeon it rivalled Byzantium, adopted Christianity under Boris I and became the cradle of Cyrillic literature, until Basil II conquered it in 1018.
summary.zh: 阿斯帕鲁赫率领保加尔人在多瑙河以南建国，突厥系保加尔贵族与斯拉夫农民逐渐融合。在克鲁姆和西美昂治下，它与拜占庭分庭抗礼；鲍里斯一世时皈依基督教，成为西里尔文学的摇篮，直到1018年被巴西尔二世征服。

sources.title: Britannica: Bulgaria: History
John V. A. Fine, The Early Medieval Balkans (1983)
Florin Curta, Southeastern Europe in the Middle Ages, 500–1250 (2006)

note: Reign dates of the early khans are approximate.

summary.en: The brothers Peter and Asen led a revolt against Byzantine taxation in 1185 and re-established Bulgaria with its capital at Tarnovo. Under Kaloyan and Ivan Asen II it defeated the Latin Empire and dominated the Balkans; weakened by Mongol raids and division, it fell to the Ottomans by 1396.
summary.zh: 1185年，彼得与阿森兄弟发动反抗拜占庭苛税的起义，重建保加利亚，定都特尔诺沃。在卡洛扬和伊凡·阿森二世治下，它击败拉丁帝国，称雄巴尔干；后因蒙古人侵袭和内部分裂而衰落，至1396年被奥斯曼人吞并。

sources.title: Britannica: Bulgaria: The Second Bulgarian Empire
John V. A. Fine, The Late Medieval Balkans (1987)

capital.zh: 维利格勒（可能为米库尔契采或旧城）

summary.en: The first major Slavic state in Central Europe arose when Mojmír I united Moravia and Nitra. Rastislav invited the Byzantine mission of Cyril and Methodius, and Svatopluk extended his rule over Bohemia and Pannonia, before the state collapsed under Magyar attacks in the early 10th century.
summary.zh: 中欧第一个重要的斯拉夫国家在莫伊米尔一世统一摩拉维亚和尼特拉后兴起。拉斯蒂斯拉夫邀请西里尔和美多德的拜占庭传教团，斯瓦托普卢克将统治扩展至波希米亚和潘诺尼亚；10世纪初，国家在马扎尔人的攻击下崩溃。

sources.title: Britannica: Great Moravia
Florin Curta, Southeastern Europe in the Middle Ages (2006)
Lumír Poláček, Great Moravia (Archaeological Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences, Brno)

note: The location of the capital is uncertain; Mikulčice is used.

capital.zh: 埃斯泰尔戈姆（10世纪后期）

summary.en: The confederation of Magyar tribes that occupied the Carpathian Basin under Árpád raided widely across Europe until defeat at the Lechfeld in 955. Grand Princes Taksony and Géza consolidated power and invited Christian missionaries, and Géza's son Stephen turned the principality into a kingdom.
summary.zh: 阿尔帕德率领的马扎尔部落联盟占据喀尔巴阡盆地后四处劫掠欧洲，直到955年在莱希费尔德战败。塔克绍尼和盖佐两位大公巩固权力并引入基督教传教士，盖佐之子斯蒂芬把大公国变成了王国。

sources.title: Britannica: Hungary: History
Pál Engel, The Realm of St Stephen (2001)

note: Dates of the early grand princes are approximate.

capital.zh: 埃斯泰尔戈姆、塞克什白堡、布达；1536—1783年为普雷斯堡

summary.en: Founded with the coronation of Stephen I, the kingdom was ruled by the Árpád dynasty, then by Angevin, Luxembourg and Hunyadi kings, and was a great power under Louis I and Matthias Corvinus. After Mohács (1526) it was divided between the Habsburgs and the Ottomans; reunited under the Habsburgs, it was a partner in Austria-Hungary from 1867 to 1918.
summary.zh: 王国随斯蒂芬一世加冕而建立，先后由阿尔帕德王朝、安茹王朝、卢森堡王朝和匈雅提家族统治，在路易一世和马加什·科尔温时期是一大强国。1526年莫哈奇战役后被哈布斯堡家族与奥斯曼帝国瓜分；在哈布斯堡治下重新统一后，1867年至1918年为奥匈帝国的组成部分。

sources.title: Britannica: Hungary: History
Pál Engel, The Realm of St Stephen (2001)
László Kontler, A History of Hungary (2002)

note: This record ends with the collapse of Austria-Hungary in 1918; Wikidata extends the kingdom to 1946, including the Horthy regency.

summary.en: The Přemyslid dukes, beginning with the Christian convert Bořivoj I, built Prague Castle and united the Czech tribes. Duke Wenceslaus, murdered by his brother in 935, became the patron saint of the Czechs; the duchy entered the Holy Roman Empire and became a hereditary kingdom in 1198.
summary.zh: 普热米斯尔王朝的公爵们从皈依基督教的博日沃伊一世开始修建布拉格城堡，统一捷克诸部落。935年被弟弟杀害的瓦茨拉夫公爵成为捷克人的主保圣人；公国并入神圣罗马帝国，1198年成为世袭王国。

name.zh: 瓦茨拉夫一世（圣瓦茨拉夫）

sources.title: Britannica: Bohemia
Lisa Wolverton, Hastening Toward Prague: Power and Society in the Medieval Czech Lands (2001)

note: The start date (c. 870, Bořivoj) is approximate.

summary.en: Raised to a hereditary kingdom in 1198, Bohemia was the richest land of the Holy Roman Empire under the Přemyslids and Luxembourgs, whose king was an imperial elector. Charles IV made Prague an imperial capital. After the Hussite century and the defeat at White Mountain (1620) it was ruled by the Habsburgs until 1918.
summary.zh: 波希米亚于1198年升为世袭王国，在普热米斯尔王朝和卢森堡王朝治下是神圣罗马帝国最富庶的领地，国王为帝国选帝侯之一。查理四世使布拉格成为帝国都城。经历胡斯派世纪和1620年白山战役失败后，它由哈布斯堡家族统治直至1918年。

sources.title: Britannica: Bohemia
Hugh Agnew, The Czechs and the Lands of the Bohemian Crown (2004)

name.zh: 皮雅斯特王朝波兰（波兰王国）

capital.zh: 格涅兹诺和波兹南，后为克拉科夫

summary.en: Mieszko I's duchy of the Polans accepted Christianity in 966, and his son Bolesław I was crowned king in 1025. After 1138 Poland split into provincial duchies; Władysław the Elbow-high reunited the core and was crowned in Kraków in 1320, and his son Casimir III the Great rebuilt the state before the Piast line ended in 1370.
summary.zh: 梅什科一世的波兰人公国于966年皈依基督教，其子波列斯瓦夫一世于1025年加冕为王。1138年后波兰分裂为诸省公国；瓦迪斯瓦夫一世（矮子）重新统一核心地区，1320年在克拉科夫加冕，其子卡齐米日三世大王重建国家，1370年皮雅斯特主系绝嗣。

name.zh: 勇敢者波列斯瓦夫一世

sources.title: Britannica: Poland: History
Norman Davies, God's Playground, vol. 1 (2005)
Paul W. Knoll, The Rise of the Polish Monarchy (1972)

note: Wikidata's Kingdom of Poland item begins with the coronation of 1025; this record starts with Mieszko I's duchy around 960.

name.en: Crown of the Kingdom of Poland (Jagiellonian)

summary.en: From the Union of Krewo the Polish crown was held by the Jagiellonian dynasty in personal union with Lithuania. Victory at Grunwald and the Thirteen Years' War against the Teutonic Order, a Renaissance golden age in Kraków and the rise of noble parliamentary government led to the Union of Lublin in 1569.
summary.zh: 自克雷沃联合起，波兰王位由雅盖隆王朝掌握，与立陶宛结成君合国。格伦瓦尔德大捷和对条顿骑士团的十三年战争、克拉科夫的文艺复兴黄金时代以及贵族议会政治的兴起，最终促成了1569年的卢布林联合。

name.zh: 瓦迪斯瓦夫二世·雅盖沃
齐格蒙特二世·奥古斯特

sources.title: Britannica: Poland: The Jagiellonian era
Norman Davies, God's Playground, vol. 1 (2005)

note: Wikidata's Crown of the Kingdom of Poland item runs to 1795; this record ends at the Union of Lublin, after which see the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

capital.en: Vilnius (from c. 1323); earlier Kernavė and Trakai
capital.zh: 维尔纽斯（约1323年起）；此前为凯尔纳维和特拉凯

summary.en: United by Mindaugas, the last pagan state of Europe expanded under Gediminas, Algirdas and Vytautas over the lands of Rus' as far as the Black Sea, becoming one of Europe's largest states. Joined to Poland by Jogaila's personal union in 1386, it adopted Catholicism and merged into the Commonwealth in 1569.
summary.zh: 明道加斯统一立陶宛后，这个欧洲最后的异教国家在格迪米纳斯、阿尔吉达斯和维陶塔斯治下扩张至罗斯诸地，直抵黑海，成为欧洲最大的国家之一。1386年通过约盖拉与波兰结成君合国，皈依天主教，1569年并入联邦。

name.zh: 齐格蒙特二世·奥古斯特

sources.title: Britannica: Lithuania: History
S. C. Rowell, Lithuania Ascending (1994)
Zigmantas Kiaupa et al., The History of Lithuania before 1795 (2000)

note: Wikidata extends the Grand Duchy to 1795, as it survived as a constituent of the Commonwealth; this record ends in 1569 to avoid overlapping polity-polish-lithuanian-commonwealth.

name.zh: 塞尔维亚王国（尼曼雅王朝）

capital.en: Ras and itinerant courts; later Skopje
capital.zh: 拉斯及巡行宫廷，后为斯科普里

summary.en: Stefan Nemanjić was crowned king in 1217 and his brother Sava founded an autocephalous Serbian church in 1219. Silver mines and the conquests of Stefan Milutin made Serbia the leading Balkan power, and its kings endowed monasteries such as Studenica, Gračanica and Visoki Dečani.
summary.zh: 斯特凡·尼曼雅于1217年加冕为王，其弟萨瓦于1219年创立自主的塞尔维亚教会。银矿财富和斯特凡·米卢廷的征服使塞尔维亚成为巴尔干的头号强国，历代国王捐建了斯图代尼察、格拉查尼察和维索基德查尼等修道院。

sources.title: Britannica: Serbia: History
John V. A. Fine, The Late Medieval Balkans (1987)

note: Ras (near Novi Pazar) is used as the capital location; the court moved frequently.

summary.en: Proclaimed when Stefan Dušan was crowned Emperor of the Serbs and Greeks at Skopje in 1346, the empire stretched from the Danube to the Gulf of Corinth. After Dušan's death it fragmented among regional lords, and the defeat of King Vukašin by the Ottomans at the Maritsa in 1371 ended it.
summary.zh: 1346年斯特凡·杜尚在斯科普里加冕为“塞尔维亚人与希腊人的皇帝”，帝国由此建立，疆域从多瑙河延伸到科林斯湾。杜尚死后，帝国被各地领主分割，1371年武卡辛国王在马里查河败于奥斯曼人，帝国随之终结。

name.zh: 武卡辛·姆尔尼亚夫切维奇（共治国王）

sources.title: Britannica: Stefan Dušan
John V. A. Fine, The Late Medieval Balkans (1987)

summary.en: Prince Lazar Hrebeljanović built the strongest of the successor states of Dušan's empire in the Morava valley. He died at Kosovo in 1389; his widow Milica and son Stefan Lazarević accepted Ottoman vassalage, and Stefan later received the Byzantine title of despot.
summary.zh: 拉扎尔·赫雷别利亚诺维奇大公在摩拉瓦河谷建立了杜尚帝国诸继承国中最强的一个。他于1389年战死科索沃；其遗孀米利察和儿子斯特凡·拉扎雷维奇接受奥斯曼宗主权，斯特凡后来获得拜占庭的“专制君主”称号。

name.zh: 拉扎尔·赫雷别利亚诺维奇

sources.title: John V. A. Fine, The Late Medieval Balkans (1987)
Wikipedia: Moravian Serbia

capital.zh: 贝尔格莱德，1430年起为斯梅代雷沃

summary.en: Stefan Lazarević, made despot by the Byzantines after the battle of Ankara, rebuilt Belgrade and fostered a late flowering of Serbian literature. Đurađ Branković built the great fortress of Smederevo, but the Ottomans took it in 1459, ending medieval Serbian statehood.
summary.zh: 安卡拉战役后，斯特凡·拉扎雷维奇获拜占庭授予“专制君主”称号，他重建贝尔格莱德，推动了塞尔维亚文学的晚期繁荣。久拉吉·布兰科维奇修建了宏伟的斯梅代雷沃要塞，但奥斯曼人于1459年攻占该城，中世纪塞尔维亚国家就此终结。

sources.title: John V. A. Fine, The Late Medieval Balkans (1987)
Britannica: Serbia: History

capital.en: Nin, Knin, Biograd and other royal seats
capital.zh: 宁、克宁、比奥格勒等王都

summary.en: Tomislav, traditionally the first king of the Croats, united Dalmatian and Pannonian Croatia around 925. The Trpimirović kings Peter Krešimir IV and Demetrius Zvonimir ruled the Adriatic coast; after a succession war the crown passed in 1102 to the kings of Hungary, in a union that lasted until 1918.
summary.zh: 传统上被视为克罗地亚首位国王的托米斯拉夫约在925年统一了达尔马提亚和潘诺尼亚克罗地亚。特尔皮米罗维奇王朝的彼得·克雷希米尔四世和德米塔尔·兹沃尼米尔统治亚得里亚海沿岸；经过继承战争，1102年王冠转归匈牙利国王，这一联合延续至1918年。

sources.title: Britannica: Croatia: History
Neven Budak, Hrvatska povijest od 550. do 1100. (2018)
John V. A. Fine, The Early Medieval Balkans (1983)

note: Tomislav's royal title rests on a papal letter of 925; Knin is used as a representative royal seat.

summary.en: In 1136 the citizens of Novgorod expelled Prince Vsevolod, and thereafter the town assembly (veche) chose its princes, posadniks and archbishops. Rich from the fur trade with the Hanseatic League, Novgorod ruled a vast northern hinterland and escaped Mongol conquest, until Ivan III annexed it in 1478.
summary.zh: 1136年诺夫哥罗德市民驱逐弗谢沃洛德大公，此后由市民大会（维彻）推选王公、市长和大主教。凭借与汉萨同盟的毛皮贸易，诺夫哥罗德富甲一方，统治着广袤的北方腹地，并躲过了蒙古人的征服，直到1478年被伊凡三世吞并。

name.zh: 弗谢沃洛德·姆斯季斯拉维奇（1136年被逐）
亚历山大·涅夫斯基（王公）
雅罗斯拉夫·雅罗斯拉维奇（王公）

sources.title: Britannica: Novgorod
Janet Martin, Medieval Russia, 980–1584 (2007)
UNESCO World Heritage: Historic Monuments of Novgorod and Surroundings

note: Novgorod had no single ruler; elected princes and the archbishop are listed as its most prominent figures.

capital.zh: 哈利奇，后为霍尔姆和利沃夫

summary.en: Roman Mstislavich united Galicia and Volhynia in 1199. His son Daniel survived the Mongol invasion as a Horde vassal, was crowned king by a papal legate in 1253 and founded Lviv. When the dynasty died out in 1340 the lands were divided between Poland and Lithuania.
summary.zh: 罗曼·姆斯季斯拉维奇于1199年统一加利西亚和沃伦。其子达尼洛作为汗国附庸度过了蒙古入侵，1253年由教宗使节加冕为王，并建立利沃夫。1340年王朝绝嗣后，其领土被波兰和立陶宛瓜分。

sources.title: Britannica: Galicia–Volhynia
Paul Robert Magocsi, A History of Ukraine (2010)
Encyclopedia of Ukraine: Galicia-Volhynia, Principality of

note: The end date varies (1340, 1349 or 1392) depending on when the Polish–Lithuanian partition is counted as complete.

summary.en: Andrey Bogolyubsky moved the senior throne of north-eastern Rus' to Vladimir, which he adorned with white-stone churches, and sacked Kiev in 1169. Devastated by the Mongols in 1238, the grand principality became a title granted by the Golden Horde, contested by Tver and Moscow until Moscow won it permanently in the 1330s.
summary.zh: 安德烈·博戈柳布斯基把东北罗斯的大公宝座迁到弗拉基米尔，以白石教堂装点这座城市，并于1169年洗劫基辅。1238年遭蒙古人蹂躏后，大公之位成为金帐汗国授予的封号，由特维尔和莫斯科争夺，直到1330年代莫斯科永久夺得。

sources.title: Britannica: Vladimir-Suzdal
Janet Martin, Medieval Russia, 980–1584 (2007)
UNESCO World Heritage: White Monuments of Vladimir and Suzdal

note: The end date is conventional: Ivan I of Moscow secured the grand-princely patent around 1331–1332.

summary.en: Set up by the Fourth Crusade after the sack of Constantinople, the Latin Empire held the city and parts of Thrace, with Venice controlling much of the trade. Its first emperor, Baldwin I, was captured by the Bulgarian tsar Kaloyan in 1205; impoverished and squeezed by Nicaea and Bulgaria, it fell to Michael VIII in 1261.
summary.zh: 拉丁帝国由第四次十字军在洗劫君士坦丁堡后建立，占据该城及色雷斯部分地区，威尼斯则控制了大部分贸易。首任皇帝鲍德温一世于1205年被保加利亚沙皇卡洛扬俘虏；帝国日渐贫困，又受尼西亚和保加利亚夹击，1261年被米海尔八世攻灭。

sources.title: Britannica: Latin Empire of Constantinople
Filip Van Tricht, The Latin Renovatio of Byzantium (2011)

summary.en: Invited by Duke Conrad of Masovia to fight the pagan Prussians, the German crusading order conquered Prussia and, through its Livonian branch, much of the eastern Baltic. Ruled from the vast brick castle of Marienburg, it was broken at Grunwald in 1410 and became a Polish fief in 1466; in 1525 its last grand master in Prussia secularised it as the Duchy of Prussia.
summary.zh: 应马佐夫舍公爵康拉德之邀前来征讨异教普鲁士人的德意志十字军骑士团，征服了普鲁士，并通过其利沃尼亚分团控制了波罗的海东岸大部。骑士团以宏伟的马林堡砖城为统治中心，1410年在格伦瓦尔德遭受重创，1466年成为波兰的藩属；1525年，其在普鲁士的末任大团长将其世俗化为普鲁士公国。

name.zh: 赫尔曼·冯·萨尔察（大团长）
勃兰登堡—安斯巴赫的阿尔布雷希特

sources.title: Britannica: Teutonic Order
William Urban, The Teutonic Knights: A Military History (2003)
UNESCO World Heritage: Castle of the Teutonic Order in Malbork

summary.en: Founded by Hacı Giray as the Golden Horde broke apart, the khanate became an Ottoman vassal in 1475. Its cavalry raided Poland-Lithuania and Muscovy for captives sold in the slave markets of Caffa, and burned Moscow in 1571. Catherine II annexed it in 1783.
summary.zh: 金帐汗国分裂之际，哈吉·格莱建立了克里米亚汗国，1475年成为奥斯曼帝国的附庸。汗国骑兵频频袭击波兰—立陶宛和莫斯科国，掳掠人口卖往卡法的奴隶市场，并于1571年火烧莫斯科。1783年叶卡捷琳娜二世将其吞并。

sources.title: Britannica: Crimean Khanate
Brian Glyn Williams, The Crimean Tatars (2015)
Alan W. Fisher, The Crimean Tatars (1978)

note: Meñli I Giray's reign was interrupted twice.

capital.zh: 奇吉林，后为巴图林和格卢霍夫

summary.en: Created by Bohdan Khmelnytsky's uprising, the Cossack state in central Ukraine accepted the Russian tsar's protection in 1654. Divided along the Dnieper after the "Ruin" of civil wars, its Left-Bank part kept autonomy under hetmans such as Ivan Mazepa, who sided with Sweden in 1708, until Catherine II abolished the office in 1764.
summary.zh: 赫梅利尼茨基起义建立了乌克兰中部的哥萨克国家，1654年接受俄国沙皇的保护。经历内战频仍的“废墟时期”后，它沿第聂伯河被一分为二，左岸部分在伊凡·马泽帕等盖特曼治下保持自治；马泽帕于1708年倒向瑞典。1764年叶卡捷琳娜二世废除了盖特曼一职。

sources.title: Britannica: Cossack
Serhii Plokhy, The Gates of Europe (2021)
Zenon E. Kohut, Russian Centralism and Ukrainian Autonomy (1988)

capital.en: Curtea de Argeș, Târgoviște, then Bucharest
capital.zh: 阿尔杰什苑、特尔戈维什泰，后为布加勒斯特

summary.en: Basarab I won independence from Hungary at Posada in 1330. Wallachia's voivodes, among them Mircea the Elder and Vlad III "the Impaler", resisted the Ottomans but accepted vassal status; Michael the Brave briefly united it with Transylvania and Moldavia in 1600. It united with Moldavia under Alexandru Ioan Cuza in 1859.
summary.zh: 巴萨拉布一世于1330年在波萨达战胜匈牙利，赢得独立。瓦拉几亚的大公们（包括老米尔恰和“穿刺者”弗拉德三世）抵抗奥斯曼人，但最终接受藩属地位；勇敢的米哈伊于1600年短暂地将其与特兰西瓦尼亚和摩尔达维亚统一。1859年它在亚历山德鲁·伊万·库扎治下与摩尔达维亚联合。

name.zh: 康斯坦丁·布伦科维亚努

sources.title: Britannica: Walachia
Keith Hitchins, A Concise History of Romania (2014)

note: The start date c. 1310 follows the beginning of Basarab I's rule; independence is dated to the battle of Posada (1330).

summary.en: Founded as a Hungarian border march and made independent by Bogdan I around 1359, Moldavia reached its height under Stephen the Great, who fought the Ottomans and built the painted monasteries of Bukovina. An Ottoman vassal from the 16th century, it lost Bessarabia to Russia in 1812 and united with Wallachia in 1859.
summary.zh: 摩尔达维亚始为匈牙利的边疆马尔克，约1359年由博格丹一世使之独立，在斯特凡大公时期达到鼎盛，他抗击奥斯曼人，并修建了布科维纳的彩绘修道院。16世纪起成为奥斯曼附庸，1812年比萨拉比亚被割给俄国，1859年与瓦拉几亚联合。

sources.title: Britannica: Moldavia
Keith Hitchins, A Concise History of Romania (2014)
UNESCO World Heritage: Churches of Moldavia

note: Suceava is used as the capital location; the start date reflects the Hungarian march under Dragoș (c. 1346–1347).

summary.en: Poland regained independence in November 1918 and fixed its borders through wars with Ukraine and Soviet Russia. A fragile parliamentary democracy gave way after Józef Piłsudski's coup of 1926 to an authoritarian Sanation regime. Germany and the Soviet Union invaded and partitioned the republic in September 1939.
summary.zh: 1918年11月波兰重获独立，通过与乌克兰和苏俄的战争确定了边界。脆弱的议会民主制在1926年毕苏斯基政变后让位于威权的“萨纳奇亚”（整顿）政权。1939年9月，德国和苏联入侵并瓜分了这个共和国。

name.zh: 约瑟夫·毕苏斯基（国家元首）
加布里埃尔·纳鲁托维奇

sources.title: Britannica: Poland: The Second Republic
Norman Davies, God's Playground, vol. 2 (2005)

summary.en: The communist state, imposed under Soviet control after the Second World War within new borders moved westward, went through the crises of 1956, 1970 and 1980. The Solidarity movement and the round-table talks of 1989 ended one-party rule; the republic was renamed the Republic of Poland in December 1989.
summary.zh: 二战后在苏联控制下建立的共产党国家，疆界整体西移，先后经历1956年、1970年和1980年的危机。团结工会运动和1989年的圆桌会谈结束了一党统治；1989年12月国名改为波兰共和国。

name.zh: 沃伊切赫·雅鲁泽尔斯基

sources.title: Britannica: Poland: Communist Poland
Andrzej Paczkowski, The Spring Will Be Ours: Poland and the Poles from Occupation to Freedom (2003)

note: Communist rule began in 1944–1945; the name was formally adopted in the 1952 constitution. 1947 marks the rigged elections and Bierut's presidency.

summary.en: Proclaimed in October 1918 with Tomáš Masaryk as president, the republic was Central Europe's most durable interwar democracy until the Munich Agreement of 1938 and German occupation. Communist from 1948, it saw the Prague Spring crushed in 1968, returned to democracy in the Velvet Revolution of 1989 and split peacefully at the end of 1992.
summary.zh: 1918年10月宣布成立，马萨里克任总统，是两次大战之间中欧最持久的民主国家，直到1938年《慕尼黑协定》和随后的德国占领。1948年起为共产党统治，1968年布拉格之春遭镇压，1989年天鹅绒革命后恢复民主，1992年底和平分立。

sources.title: Britannica: Czechoslovakia
Mary Heimann, Czechoslovakia: The State That Failed (2009)

summary.en: The Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes formed in 1918 was renamed Yugoslavia in 1929 under King Alexander's dictatorship. Occupied and torn by civil war in 1941–1945, it was rebuilt by Tito's Partisans as a socialist federation that broke with Stalin in 1948. After Tito's death, nationalism and economic crisis led to its violent break-up from 1991.
summary.zh: 1918年成立的塞尔维亚人、克罗地亚人和斯洛文尼亚人王国于1929年在亚历山大国王独裁下改名南斯拉夫。1941—1945年遭占领并陷入内战，战后由铁托的游击队重建为社会主义联邦，1948年与斯大林决裂。铁托去世后，民族主义和经济危机导致其自1991年起暴力解体。

sources.title: Britannica: Yugoslavia
John R. Lampe, Yugoslavia as History: Twice There Was a Country (2nd ed. 2000)

summary.en: Independent since August 1991, Ukraine went through the Orange Revolution of 2004 and the Revolution of Dignity of 2014. Russia annexed Crimea and backed separatists in the Donbas in 2014, and launched a full-scale invasion in February 2022.
summary.zh: 乌克兰自1991年8月独立，经历了2004年的橙色革命和2014年的尊严革命。2014年俄罗斯吞并克里米亚并支持顿巴斯分离武装，2022年2月发动全面入侵。

sources.title: Britannica: Ukraine
Serhii Plokhy, The Gates of Europe (2021)

note: Wikidata's item for the country has no 1991 start date; the record covers the independent state.

summary.en: The successor state of the Soviet Union went through shock-therapy economic reform, the constitutional crisis of 1993 and wars in Chechnya under Boris Yeltsin. Under Vladimir Putin power was recentralised; Russia fought Georgia in 2008, annexed Crimea in 2014 and invaded Ukraine in 2022.
summary.zh: 作为苏联的继承国，俄罗斯在叶利钦时期经历了“休克疗法”式经济改革、1993年宪政危机和车臣战争。普京执政后权力重新集中；俄罗斯于2008年与格鲁吉亚交战，2014年吞并克里米亚，2022年入侵乌克兰。
